newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns IRA attack in Belfast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns IRA attack in Belfast.

text.p: The United States condemned the IRA attack on Northern Ireland's Courts of Justice on Monday and warned that such incidents could complicate multi-party peace talks sheduled to resume later this month.
Washington also urged all sides to "show restraint and give peace negotiations a chance to succeed," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

"The United States condemns in the strongest terms the attack on the Belfast courthouse today," Burns said, adding it followed discoveries of apparent Irish Republican Army bombs being prepared for "terrorist attacks."
"These incidents have shaken the fragile peace in Northern Ireland and continued violence could complicate the multi-party talks which are scheduled to resume later this month," he said.
"The United States shares the hope expressed by the British and Irish governments that these incidents will not provoke (Protestant) loyalist groups to end their ceasefire," Burns said.

A "propelled recoilless improvised grenade (PRIG)" -- part of the IRA's armoury of home-made weapons -- was fired from a car passing the heavily protected court complex, the heart of Britain's legal system in Northern Ireland regarded by the guerrillas as a prestige target. A policeman was wounded.
